narrative:
The model predicted a 67% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were your undergraduate GPA, your first-year law school grades, and your LSAT score. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.80 was the strongest influence; it sits noticeably below the 3.23 average of students who were accepted, and this lower performance pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year grades, which placed you in the third decile compared with an average of sixth decile among accepted students, also pulled the outcome toward rejection. These two academic signals together created the largest part of the model’s concern.

Your LSAT score of 40 worked in the opposite direction. It is higher than the 37.18 average of accepted students and therefore nudged the prediction toward passing. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not large enough to overcome the academic performance indicators.

Because the decision rested primarily on your undergraduate record and early law school grades, the clearest next step is to strengthen your academic profile. Consider retaking key courses, enrolling in a structured academic support program, or gaining additional professional experience that demonstrates your ability to handle rigorous legal study. Improving in these areas will give future applications a much stronger foundation. (248 words)
